headline: Medium-risk pair: Dagster can feed untrusted pipeline output into Rasa, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct shared-channel evidence for higher severity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster can orchestrate data pipelines and produce outputs that Rasa may ingest through chat or API integrations. Rasa exposes multiple messaging channels, so if Dagster writes attacker-controlled content into a shared handoff, Rasa could treat it as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are routed into a Rasa channel or training/input file without sanitization
IF Rasa parses pipeline-produced text as conversational instructions
mitigations: Add an allowlist filter on Dagster-produced text before it reaches Rasa
Insert a human review step for any pipeline content that becomes bot input
Prefix all machine-generated content with non-executable metadata
requires-engineering: separate the Dagster and Rasa handoff with a provenance-aware queue

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is documented with no filesystem read/write or network egress, while Rasa has allowlisted egress and text/voice handling. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is plausible only through an external integration path, not by default.
conditions: IF an operator connects Dagster outputs containing sensitive text to a Rasa channel
IF Rasa is configured to forward that text to an external API
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of Dagster task outputs
Disable any Rasa connector that forwards raw message text externally
Redact secrets before handoff between systems
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data classification at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster has no filesystem write, shell, or network egress in the profile, while Rasa only shows allowlisted egress and no multi-instance support. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface documented, so a direct capability conflict is not supported.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database
mitigations: Keep Dagster and Rasa on separate service accounts
Avoid mounting a shared writable volume
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can generate pipeline outputs that Rasa may consume as dialogue content, and Rasa's channel integrations can act on that content without an explicit verification layer in the profile. That creates a realistic path where Dagster errors or hallucinated facts cascade into user-facing bot responses. The interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dagster output is used as Rasa training data, FAQ content, or live response text
IF Rasa does not verify the content before replying
mitigations: Add a validation step before Dagster output is consumed by Rasa
Require source citations for any generated facts
Route uncertain outputs to a fallback response
requires-engineering: add automated regression tests for pipeline-to-bot handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster's profile shows no touched data classes or requested secrets, while Rasa touches text and voice and can connect to external messaging APIs. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to a small, integration-specific gap rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated text or voice data is routed from Dagster into a Rasa connector with different retention rules
mitigations: Confirm retention settings on each Rasa channel
Avoid sending regulated data through the bot path
Document the data class allowed at the integration boundary
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
